children: The oil price shock triggered by the ongoing war with Iran is proving more severe and prolonged than the market fallout from Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, according to Wall Street financier Steve Rattner.
In contrast, the 2026 war between the U.S., Israel and Iran has kept crude prices substantially elevated, remaining well above baseline levels through 219 days of hostilities.
Despite the sustained market shock, WTI fell back to below $100 per barrel this week, changing hands around $92.50 as of Friday midafternoon trading, on
amid reports Iran has proposed a plan to end the conflict. Under the offer, the Strait of Hormuz would reopen and nuclear discussions would be restored.

title: Iran war oil shock outliving Ukraine fallout
